restriction: される is the short causative-passive, and only godan verbs other than す-verbs have one: 書かされる, 飲まされる. Other verbs use causative then passive: 食べさせられる, 話させられる.
meaning: Short causative-passive: be made to do.

examples.japanese: 先生に長い時間待たされた。
examples.reading: せんせいにながいじかんまたされた。
examples.gloss: The teacher kept me waiting a long time.

examples.japanese: 子供のころ、毎日ピアノを習わされた。
examples.reading: こどものころ、まいにちピアノをならわされた。
examples.gloss: As a child, I was made to take piano lessons every day.

examples.japanese: 飲み会で無理やりお酒を飲まされた。
examples.reading: のみかいでむりやりおさけをのまされた。
examples.gloss: At the party I was forced to drink alcohol.

usage: A shorter way to say the causative-passive for godan verbs: 書かせられる becomes 書かされる. Both are correct, and the short form is the more usual one in speech.
Only godan verbs other than す-verbs have it. 話す has just 話させられる, because 話される is the plain passive. Ichidan and irregular verbs use the long form: 食べさせられる, させられる, 来させられる.
It often carries the feeling of being forced or put out: 待たされた is 'I was kept waiting'.

compare.label: させられる (long form)
compare.difference: The long form is built from the causative and then the passive, so every verb has it: 書かせられる, 食べさせられる. It is a little more formal and takes a moment longer to say.
The plain passive is 書かれる, 'be written'. The short causative-passive 書かされる is 'be made to write'.
